poster.note: Strong. 'Buqu howls across the sunset' reads from the 685x343 hero down to 90x70, the dusk sun is the visible light source, and the 2:3, 1:1 and 9:16 versions are recomposed rather than cropped. The bottom 26 px are mist and peak bodies, with no ember in the bottom 120 px. Minor: the ink ring, hair cap and braid can read as a glass helmet and hose at thumbnail size, but that is the game's own sprite.

focus.note: Focus 0.55,0.38 is on the face. wall.py keeps the whole head from the 577x163 strip to the 140x305 column, and the 4:3 crop keeps the face and sun.

icon.note: Drawn for 46, not shrunk: topknot, ringed glaring head, crimson frill. Reads at 1x on night and on linen, with sharp corners and no text. One of the best pieces.

emblem.note: Fewer parts than the icon (no nose, no drips) and its own layout. The two eyes stay separate at 30 px.

chip.note: The icon's parts plus the braid. More than the icon and less than the poster, and it reads at 64.

keyStill.note: Real tension (two net guards close in while he glares back), subject centred, one sun drawn. Three shapes survive at 132x66.

result.note: The landing after a long flight, with the trail arc and head in the middle 720. No text or seals. The guarded gorge sun sits top right, outside the middle.

gallery.note: Six real autopilot frames from the build, in the game's own renderer, so the finish is right. Each subject holds in the central 4:3 (checked), and the bottom 26 px are calm. Weakest pair: 01 and 04 share the parade, noon sky and rainbow. Consider another character beat, such as a net guard on the Stair, for 04.

seals.note: 'every-hidden-seal' carves the game's chop strokes, which read as an 'S'/'5' with dashes at 96 and 48 px: text inside the seal (the pass itself left sealTex out of the result and gallery for this reason). Carve a non-letter glyph. The other eight seals and the three outlines read well at 32. Mirror Lake reads a little like a watermelon slice.

store.note: Four looks-only items on the world's grounds, each readable at 40 px, in black fill and in greyscale. Calm top corners, no gold, guarded game colours moved to free neighbours.

passTile.note: The step unit (a span between two towers) is the picture. The name reads from 120 px and its 125 px minimum is stated. No price or count.

passGrounds.note: Cream, jade and dusk indigo: light, mid and dark, clearly three tiers.

marker.note: A paper lantern from the world, drawn for 48. 'Next' swings and 'held' is set down and lit. The difference is subtle but present.

passRewards.note: All eight read at 120 px, full art, tier shown by the ground only, no counts or crumbs. The jade row's contour lines are busy behind the thinner items (cloud ribbon, magpie), but still readable.

owned.note: 'Laid': a crimson tessera pressed into grout. The module (720 ms, once, ends on held()) and reward-held.png are both there, and the held frame reads at 40 px. No gold.

update.note: The change (a rocket fizzling against masonry) doesn't read: no rocket or wall contact is visible, the burst sits in pale haze about 90 px below the bricks, and at 104x52 it is a washed-out blob (L 0.92). Restage or reframe on a wall face where head, rocket and bricks touch in frame, ideally on a darker ground.

event.note: A good night variant, clearly different from the poster, with a round-ring event seal in three states. But a banner pole and two crimson seal chops whose strokes read as letters sit right on the 45% line beside the copy and Join. Hide them, as the pass did elsewhere, so the left 45% edge is clean.

living.note: Rendered it myself in Chromium: no errors, recomposes from 120x90 to 900x640 and 140x305 without bars, anchor() on the face, the held/rm frame is the poster, and the idle, react, loop and squeezed modes are all present. Loop frames reach about 2.8 ms in software GL, so check on real hardware. It is a Canvas port of the game's code (the contract allows only Canvas 2D).

backdrop.note: Last Gate at dusk, at rest, ending on the wall walk and moat. The phone version is composed separately. The warm gatehouse sits under the hero slot, so the poster leads.

share.note: At the 270 px link preview, the English line 'BUQU WILL / NOT BOW' has caps about 10 px, below the 12 px lettering minimum. Enlarge it to caps of about 53 px or more on the 1200 master, or drop it and let 不屈 carry the title. The braid's end also crowds 'BOW'. Register, subject at 0.755 and the quiet bottom band are right.

phone.note: Recomposed for 9:16 around the head and sun, with the same register as the 2:1.

lockup.note: The game's own fonts filled with the game's tesserae. Minimum widths are stated (134 px readable, 201 px recommended). Keep it off linen, where the white letters vanish.

overall: A very strong, honest pass. Every world is the game's own renderer and every character is the game's own mosaic code, so the set looks like one game in one medium, and the poster survives every wall shape. Four fixes remain: the update close-up doesn't show its change, the share card's English line is under the 12 px minimum at 270, and the letter-like chop strokes appear on one seal and at the event banner's 45% line.
made: Code, inside the game. Worlds, gallery, stills, backdrops, update and event were rendered by the game's own WebGL renderer (dist/test.html via look.mjs/shot.mjs). The gallery frames are real seeded autopilot runs. Heads, guards, seals, marks and store/pass art were drawn with the game's mosaic code (Draw + tessellate + palette) and composited with Python/Pillow. The title letters were traced from the game's fonts with Pillow. The moving poster and owned mark are hand-ported Canvas 2D modules. No image generator was used.
